solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Permit eaten by lively horse (8)

indicators.note: Whatever is eaten by something ends up inside it, so the first piece goes inside the second.

blocks.note: gay in its old sense of lively and cheerful

annotation.surface: A lively horse is caught gobbling up a permit.
annotation.walkthrough: GAY is used in its older sense of merry or lively, which crosswords still lean on.
annotation.definitionFit: Named for its home region: the Galloway was a small, hardy breed of pony from south-west Scotland.

entries.clue: Note gold chests, reduced by half, unpolished? (6)

indicators.note: Something reduced by half has lost half its size, so only half the word's letters survive.

blocks.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
CHESTS is six letters; its first three survive

annotation.surface: Someone notes that the gold chests have been halved and look rough.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark hints that 'unpolished' is about manners, not metal.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym borrowed from French, where gauche means left-handed, hence clumsy and socially unpolished.

entries.clue: Rubbish article, so long (2-2)

annotation.surface: Someone waves off a piece of junk with a farewell.
annotation.walkthrough: Tat is British slang for tasteless junk; ta-ta is an informal British goodbye.
annotation.definitionFit: Two casual farewells: so long is the American-flavoured one, ta-ta the British nursery one.

entries.clue: Grilled sandwiches secretary served up at home repeatedly (6)

indicators.note: In a down clue, something sent up rises from the bottom, so its letters read upwards, i.e. reversed.
Something done repeatedly happens more than once, so the phrase before it is written twice.

blocks.note: a PA is a personal assistant

annotation.surface: A secretary keeps bringing toasted sandwiches to people at home.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Served up' fits the food surface but is the reversal for IN IN, which turns to NI NI.
annotation.definitionFit: An Italian plural: a panino is a bread roll, and pressed, toasted ones are sold as panini.

entries.clue: Broken chord affected Georgia around piano (8)

indicators.note: Something affected has been acted on and changed, so the letters are rearranged.
Letters placed around another piece surround it, so the P sits inside the rearranged name.

annotation.surface: A broken chord moves Georgia, who is standing at the piano.
annotation.walkthrough: The music surface is real: the definition describes exactly the thing a pianist plays.
annotation.definitionFit: A musical term: an arpeggio plays a chord's notes one after another, so the chord is broken up.

entries.clue: Losing head, distant daughter expressed strong feelings (6)

indicators.note: A word losing its head loses its top, and the top of a word is its first letter.

blocks.note: REMOTE without its first letter R

annotation.surface: A daughter, estranged and not thinking straight, lets her feelings out.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Losing head' belongs to the word after it, distant, not to the daughter.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to emote is to display emotion, often theatrically.

entries.clue: Strongman regularly displayed loose costume (4)

indicators.note: Something done regularly happens at even intervals, so take letters at a steady step, here every second one.

annotation.surface: A circus strongman shows off in a baggy outfit.
annotation.walkthrough: The strongman in a loose robe looks like a classical statue, which suits the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: A historical garment: the Roman toga was a loose draped wrap, now mostly worn as fancy dress.

entries.clue: Novel in a middle-class setting, whichever way you read it (3,4)

indicators.note: A word you can read whichever way gives the same result from either end, so the letters are arranged symmetrically.

blocks.note: The definition end: a genre of fiction set in comfortable English country homes.

annotation.surface: A book set among the middle classes, readable from either end.
annotation.walkthrough: AGASAGA reads the same both ways. An Aga is a large cast-iron range cooker, a symbol of the English middle-class country kitchen.
annotation.definitionFit: A genre label coined in the 1990s for novels of English middle-class domestic life, the kind of house with an Aga in the kitchen.

entries.clue: Lover more energised by love (5)

indicators.note: Letters that are energised are stirred up and bounce about, so they are rearranged.
One thing by another stands beside it, so the pieces sit side by side.

annotation.surface: A lover finds himself more energetic thanks to love.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is itself a description of the answer, so the definition and wordplay share one picture.
annotation.definitionFit: A name turned common noun: Shakespeare's Romeo became the byword for an ardent male lover.

entries.clue: Synthetic material carefully crafted somewhat (5)

indicators.note: Somewhat means to some extent, so only some of the phrase is used: a run of letters inside it.

annotation.surface: A man-made fabric that has been made with some care.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Crafted' fits the fabric surface, which hides that the two words are only a letter source.
annotation.definitionFit: A trade name that became generic: Lycra is the stretchy man-made fibre in sportswear.

entries.clue: In charge, Ted distributed each cold drink (4,3)

indicators.note: Things distributed are spread out and handed round, so the letters end up in a new order.

annotation.surface: Ted is put in charge of handing a cold drink to everyone.
annotation.walkthrough: Ted looks like a person but is only three letters to rearrange.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by type: tea brewed and chilled over ice is one kind of cold drink.

entries.clue: Combat sport, with others against Heather (9)

indicators.note: One thing against another is pressed up next to it, so the pieces are placed side by side.

annotation.surface: A team takes on Heather at a combat sport.
annotation.walkthrough: The capital H makes Heather look like an opponent's name; it is the plant, called ling.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by category: grappling an opponent to the mat is one of the oldest unarmed fighting sports.

entries.clue: Most shabby equestrian gear spoiled site (8)

indicators.note: Something spoiled has been damaged out of its proper shape, so its letters are rearranged.

blocks.note: tack is saddle, bridle and other riding gear

annotation.surface: Riding gear left strewn across a ruined site looks at its most tatty.
annotation.walkthrough: Tack is the horse-riding term, short for tackle; the superlative ending comes from the rearranged SITE.
annotation.definitionFit: A superlative synonym: tacky means cheap and shoddy, so the tackiest thing is the most shabby.

entries.clue: Inspector initially praised hummus maybe (3)

indicators.note: Initially means at the start, so only the first letter of the next word is taken.

annotation.surface: A police inspector compliments someone's hummus.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Maybe' marks hummus as one example of the answer rather than a synonym.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: hummus is one of the things you scoop up with bread or crudités.

entries.clue: In France, ready to eat good bread with child (8)

indicators.note: What one word eats it takes inside itself, so the next pieces go within it.

annotation.surface: A French diner is about to tuck into good bread with a child.
annotation.walkthrough: 'With child' looks like part of the meal but is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: An old-fashioned idiom: a woman with child is expecting a baby.

entries.clue: The old wide tree (3)

blocks.note: ye is an old spelling of the

annotation.surface: An old spreading tree.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Ye olde' shop signs are where the old 'ye' for 'the' survives.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by category: the yew is a dark evergreen common in English churchyards.

entries.clue: Our group record current English film of great sentiment? (6)

blocks.note: an EP is an extended-play record
I is the symbol for electric current

annotation.surface: A group records a sentimental English film.
annotation.walkthrough: Weepie is informal British slang; the question mark flags the loose definition.
annotation.definitionFit: An informal term: a tear-jerker made to make its audience cry is nicknamed for the weeping.

entries.clue: Reptile circled wildly trapping two separate ducks (9)

indicators.note: Something moving wildly is out of control, so the letters are thrown into a new order.
A word trapping others holds them inside, so the extra letters sit within the rearranged ones.

blocks.note: a duck is a zero score in cricket, O; the two O's end up apart

annotation.surface: A reptile circles frantically and grabs two ducks.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Separate' tells you the two O's do not sit together in the answer: CR-O-C-O-DILE.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by category: the crocodile is one of the large armoured reptiles of the rivers.

entries.clue: Monstrous woman’s forward movement pushing away priest (6)

indicators.note: Pushing something away gets rid of it, so the named letters are removed.

blocks.note: Pr = priest; taken away from the front

annotation.surface: A woman shoves past a priest as she barges ahead.
annotation.walkthrough: The 's reads as a possessive but stands for 'is', linking the definition to the wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: A feminine form: the ogre of fairy tales is a monster, and ogress is the female of the species.

entries.clue: International performance having no breaks (6)

annotation.surface: A show performed abroad without an interval.
annotation.walkthrough: 'No breaks' suggests an uninterrupted show; it means unbroken.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: from Latin for untouched, whole and undamaged, with nothing broken.

entries.clue: Comparatively undersized baby perhaps that is in care of doctor (7)

indicators.note: Something in the care of another is held by it, so the first piece sits inside the second.

blocks.note: wee = tiny, as a baby is

annotation.surface: A small baby is in a doctor's care.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Care of' makes it look like the address abbreviation c/o, but it just means held by the doctor.
annotation.definitionFit: A comparative synonym: weedy means puny and thin, like an overgrown weed, so weedier is more undersized.

entries.clue: Insect is no longer quiet (4)

blocks.note: what is no longer 'is' has become 'was'

annotation.surface: An insect has stopped being quiet and starts buzzing.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Is no longer' reads as a statement but means the past tense of is.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by category: the striped, stinging picnic pest is one insect among many.

entries.clue: Delightful covers to mattress (5)

indicators.note: Something that covers another wraps round it, so the second piece sits inside the first.

annotation.surface: Lovely bedcovers for a mattress.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Covers' looks like bedding next to mattress but is the container.
annotation.definitionFit: A borrowing from Japanese: the traditional thin floor mattress, now also a sofa-bed.

entries.clue: Handled fabric (4)

blocks.note: touched with the hands, past tense
a cloth made by pressing wool fibres together

annotation.surface: Someone has handled a piece of cloth.
annotation.walkthrough: The two senses are unrelated words that happen to share a spelling.
annotation.definitionFit: Both senses hold: the past tense of feel means handled, and the noun is a matted woollen cloth.

entries.clue: European is following wife into ship (5)

indicators.note: One thing following another comes after it, so IS is written after W.
Something put into another goes inside it, so the pair sits within the ship.

annotation.surface: A European boards a ship after his wife.
annotation.walkthrough: 'European' is a noun here, a person from one particular country.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by category: a native of Switzerland is one kind of European.

entries.clue: Simon, fifty-one, joins Tory element (7)

blocks.note: Si is a short form of Simon

annotation.surface: Simon, now fifty-one, signs up to a faction of the Tory party.
annotation.walkthrough: Tory is the nickname of the British Conservative Party, abbreviated Con.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by category: number 14 in the periodic table, the stuff of computer chips, is a chemical element.
